statusText:
The CME weekend halt still defines the whole assessment. NQ has not quoted since Friday's close and does not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August - which, for the first time, now falls inside this 24-hour forecast window rather than beyond it. Tail is 12% (low), the action is EA_ON and the status is green, because a pathological one-way price path cannot form while no venue is quoting.

This hour sharpened the Lebanon picture rather than escalating it. The Times of Israel account adds that the trigger was a Hezbollah drone attack that seriously wounded three IDF soldiers on the Ali al-Taher ridge, and that the Israeli strikes targeted a named battalion commander, Ali Samir Al-Haj Hassan, at what the IDF calls a military headquarters where his family was present. Casualties are consistently reported as 11 dead - seven in Ansar including three children and two women, four in Deir al-Zahrani - with roughly 19 wounded. Hezbollah promises an 'appropriate' response and is pressing Beirut to abandon the 'humiliating' negotiations; President Aoun reads the strikes as a message timed ahead of the US-sponsored Rome round, and Prime Minister Salam has demanded Israel halt the escalation. The important nuance for scoring: the talks are still described as scheduled, not cancelled. That is why Stress moves only one point, to 68% (high), instead of jumping.

The Hormuz backdrop is unchanged and remains the structural energy risk: further vessel attacks including a projectile strike on a bulk carrier hull reported to UKMTO, transits collapsed to a small fraction of the roughly 130 pre-conflict daily crossings, Washington readying additional economic measures, and Tehran conditioning any reopening on sanctions relief and war reparations. Every hard mark was re-verified this hour and every one is still Friday's: NQ 30,141.75 (-0.15%, range 30,028.50-30,283.00), VIX 14.25 (-2.60%, range 14.18-14.72), WTI $82.40 (+1.42%) and Brent $88.52 (+1.67%). A 14-handle VIX against that tape is the central unresolved divergence, and it gets resolved in Sunday's reopening auction, not before.
recommendation: Base strategies stay enabled: Tail 12% maps to EA_ON. There is nothing to trade into and nothing to defend against while the venue is shut - existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The one change worth acting on is scheduling: the roughly 22:00 UTC Sunday CME restart has now entered the forecast horizon as its final slot, where forecast Tail steps to 20% and the forecast status turns yellow. Treat that thin opening auction as the single checkpoint - it is where a full weekend of two-sided Middle East headlines, a promised Hezbollah retaliation and an ongoing Hormuz blockade get priced at once. This is general market-state analysis for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice.
headline: Weekend halt keeps Tail at 12% and status green; Lebanon detail firms up (drone attack on IDF troops, named commander targeted, talks still scheduled) so Stress edges to 68% with Sunday's 22:00 UTC restart now inside the window
body:
Price path: none exists. The entire current hour and all but the last slot of the forecast sit inside the CME weekend halt, so there is no session direction, no gap, no retracement structure, no failed pullback and no proximity to extremes to score. Every price input is a Friday close carried forward. That is simultaneously the correct reason for Tail to be low and the correct reason for Confidence to sit at 66% (solid) rather than higher.

Friday's marks, all re-verified against primary sources this hour: NQ September futures 30,141.75, down 46.75 points or 0.15%, having traded 30,028.50 to 30,283.00 against a 30,188.50 previous close - a narrow, unremarkable range with no directional efficiency worth scoring, and the quote page explicitly reports the contract closed. VIX 14.25, down 2.60%, range 14.18-14.72. WTI $82.40 (+1.42%) and Brent $88.52 (+1.67%), both firm on the week with Hormuz still effectively shut. US 2-year 4.15% and 10-year 4.63% from the Fed's own H.15 release at the 13 August observation. Nothing in that cross-asset set is aligned into a one-way structure; if anything it conflicts, and conflicting signals belong in Stress, not Tail.

Geopolitics is the only live variable and this hour it gained resolution rather than momentum. The Lebanon exchange is now clearly two-sided and sequenced: a Hezbollah drone attack seriously wounded three Israeli soldiers on the Ali al-Taher ridge inside the zone Israeli troops still occupy; Israel struck Ansar and Deir al-Zahrani overnight, killing 11 including three children and two women and wounding about 19, and says it was targeting a named Hezbollah battalion commander at a military headquarters. Hezbollah promises an 'appropriate' response and is publicly pressuring Beirut to abandon negotiations. Lebanon's president and prime minister both condemned the strikes, with Aoun framing them as a message timed ahead of the US-sponsored Rome round. Separately, Hormuz remains the structural energy risk: fresh vessel attacks including a reported projectile strike on a bulk carrier, transits collapsed from roughly 130 a day pre-conflict to single digits on recent days, the US preparing further measures to force Iranian capitulation, and Araghchi conditioning reopening on sanctions relief and reparations. None of this is priced, because nothing is trading.

Why Tail stays at 12% and not higher: Tail measures a pathological price path, not the size of a pending headline stack. There is no path. The full amplifier checklist - persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, NQ pinned near an extreme, aligned yields, VIX, oil, semis, megacaps and breadth - is unobservable and stays unobservable for another twenty-two and a half hours. Publishing an elevated Tail now would assert structure that no venue has produced.

Why Stress is 68% and moves only one point: the case for holding it high is unchanged - a promised retaliation, an ongoing Hormuz blockade, further US economic measures in preparation, and a 14-handle VIX that has discounted none of it, in a market with no mechanism to reprice until Sunday night. The case against escalating it harder is this hour's actual new information: the strike reads as a targeted reprisal for a specific Hezbollah attack rather than the opening of a new campaign, and the Rome track is still described as scheduled. Compounding, not escalation, is what justifies the single point.

What is genuinely new this hour is the horizon geometry. At 23:00 UTC the 24-hour forecast now extends to 22:00 UTC Sunday, so the CME restart sits in the final slot instead of an hour beyond the edge. Forecast Tail therefore steps from 12% to 20% across the last few slots and the final slot's forecast status turns yellow (WATCH) - a thin opening auction absorbing a whole weekend at once is exactly the configuration where gap continuation can outrun mean reversion. That is a conditional forecast, not an observation: the current published action remains EA_ON and green.

Confidence at 66% (solid) reflects an honest split. The macro calendar, index, volatility, energy and rate marks are all verified against primary sources this hour and are internally consistent, and the seven-day US calendar was re-read directly from Trading Economics. But the single most informative input for a mean-reversion strategy - live price path - is structurally unavailable until the restart.

lookbackSummary: The trailing 24 hours run from 23:00 UTC Friday to 22:00 UTC Saturday and are entirely post-close. Claude published in every one of those hours. Tail never left the low band: 2% immediately after the weekly close, 9-10% through the Saturday Asian and European hours, and 11-12% into the Saturday evening. Stress is what actually moved - 12% right after the close, stepping to 45% once the weekend geopolitical picture was scored properly, then climbing monotonically through the Saturday news cycle at 48%, 50%, 53%, 55%, 58%, 60%, 62%, 65% and 67% as the Lebanon strikes were confirmed and turned into a two-sided exchange. Confidence rebuilt in parallel from 37% to 66% as primary-source marks were re-verified hour by hour. Action was EA_ON and status green for all 24 hours; dominantMode was normal for the first slot and mixed for the remaining 23.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours end at 22:00 UTC Sunday, which is the CME restart itself - so for the first time the reopen is inside the window rather than beyond it. Tail is held in the low band for 23 of 24 slots, drifting 12% to 18% as the restart approaches, then stepping to 20% for the 22:00 UTC slot, where the forecast action becomes WATCH and the forecast status yellow. Stress grinds from 68% to 75% because unpriced weekend headline risk compounds rather than decays while the venue is shut: a promised Hezbollah retaliation, an ongoing Hormuz blockade with fresh vessel attacks, and a US economic package in preparation all remain outstanding against a 14-handle VIX. Confidence eases from 66% to 61% as Friday's marks age past 70 hours with nothing newer to test them. The last four slots switch to event/whipsaw to reflect a thin opening auction that has to absorb the entire weekend at once.

forecastDetail.comment: Saturday 23:00-24:00 UTC is deep inside the CME weekend halt. NQ has not quoted since Friday's 21:00 UTC close, so no pathological price path can form and Tail holds at 12% with EA_ON. Stress ticks to 68% because this hour added a named IDF target and a promised Hezbollah response without resolving anything.

The first hour of Sunday UTC remains a dead tape. Nothing can be observed, confirmed or invalidated; Tail is unchanged at 12% and Stress holds at 68% while the unpriced weekend headline stack simply carries forward.
Asian Sunday pre-dawn. Still no venue quoting NQ and no FX or cash reference to triangulate from, so Confidence eases one point to 65% as Friday's marks age. Risk scores unchanged.

Mid Sunday-night UTC. The only realistic path to a score change is a fresh Middle East headline, not price structure. Tail stays 12%; Stress 68% reflects a live retaliation threat against a 14-handle VIX that has priced none of it.

Sunday morning UTC. Stress edges to 69% purely on time-to-reopen: every hour the halt persists is another hour of headline accumulation with no mechanism to discount it. Tail is still unobservable and stays low.

Late Sunday morning UTC, roughly fifteen hours before the CME restart. Scores hold; the entire risk profile of this window is a queue waiting for the 22:00 UTC auction rather than anything happening now.
